Formulation  
Patient presents with a six-week history of left ear hearing difficulty accompanied by intermittent tinnitus and mild dizziness without severe vertigo or associated systemic symptoms. Possible causes include impacted earwax or underlying ear pathology. No mental health concerns or psychological factors were identified or discussed during the consultation. The plan is to exclude common reversible causes and provide patient education on tinnitus. Patient demonstrates insight and willingness to engage with assessment and education materials.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Left ear hearing difficulty with tinnitus and mild dizziness  
- Patient Goal(s): To improve hearing and reduce symptoms of tinnitus and dizziness by identifying and treating the underlying cause.  
- Clinical Goal(s): To conduct an otoscopic examination to exclude impacted wax or other causes of hearing loss and tinnitus and to provide appropriate management thereafter.  
- Actions (Patient): Attend scheduled face-to-face clinic appointment for ear examination; review provided tinnitus information leaflet.  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange urgent (within 4-5 days) face-to-face ear examination in clinic; provide tinnitus educational material; review findings and determine further management.  

Secondary Problem: Not applicable  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Tinnitus explanation, potential causes, limited treatment options, advice on avoiding improper ear cleaning.  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Not recorded  
- Coping Strategies: Provided educational leaflet on tinnitus for patient to read.
